job.title: Senior Account Manager
job.description:
People2people are partnering exclusively with an established, forward-thinking digital agency based in the Perth CBD to recruit a Senior Account Manager.

This is an excellent opportunity to join a close-knit, collaborative team that combines creative expertise with advanced technology to deliver exceptional outcomes for its clients.

The Opportunity

Reporting to the Managing Director, you will take ownership of approximately 10 key client accounts, acting as the main point of contact and ensuring the successful delivery of digital projects and campaigns.

This is a pure account management role, allowing you to focus on building strong client relationships, managing projects and delivering results, without the pressure of business development or sales targets.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Manage and develop relationships with a portfolio of key clients.
  • Act as the primary point of contact for client enquiries, projects and campaigns.
  • Coordinate internal designers, developers and digital specialists to ensure projects are delivered on time and to a high standard.
  • Oversee project timelines, deliverables and client expectations.
  • Identify opportunities to improve client outcomes through digital solutions and technology.
  • Work closely with the Managing Director and wider team to maintain exceptional client service.
  • Ensure accuracy, attention to detail and accountability across all client projects.

About You

We are looking for someone who genuinely understands the digital agency environment and can confidently manage client relationships while coordinating multiple projects.

To be successful, you will have:

  • Previous account management experience within a digital agency – essential.
  • A strong understanding of digital marketing, technology and digital project delivery.
  • Excellent communication and relationship management skills.
  • Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities.
  • Exceptional attention to detail and a proactive approach to problem-solving.
  • Confidence working with designers, developers and other technical specialists.
  • An interest in emerging technologies, particularly AI and its application within digital marketing.
  • A collaborative, adaptable personality suited to a relaxed, close-knit team.

What's on Offer

  • Competitive salary: Up to $110,000 + superannuation, depending on experience.
  • Bonus opportunity: Approximately 10%, linked to individual KPIs and company performance.
  • Hybrid flexibility: Work from home Tuesdays and Thursdays, with office days Monday, Wednesday and Friday.
  • Northbridge location: Join a collaborative team in a convenient inner-city location.
  • Innovative environment: Work with advanced AI technology and internally developed digital platforms.
  • Career development: Ongoing opportunities to expand your technical knowledge and professional capabilities.
  • Great team culture: Enjoy a relaxed, social and supportive workplace that celebrates success.

About the Business

Our client is an established digital agency combining creative thinking, digital marketing and advanced technical capabilities to deliver innovative solutions for its clients.

With the backing of a leading Australian technology development business, the agency is investing heavily in AI, automation and proprietary platforms to remain at the forefront of the industry.

You will join a small, experienced team where your contributions are valued, your ideas are welcomed and you will have the opportunity to work closely with senior leadership.

Apply Now

If you have a background in digital agency account management and are looking for an opportunity to work with an innovative, technology-driven business, we would love to hear from you.

Apply now or contact Hannah Doyle at people2people on 08 6160 6210 or hannahd@people2people.com.au for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Coffee Roaster/ Production Operator
job.description:
We are currently recruiting for a Coffee Roaster / Production Operator to join an established food manufacturing business.

This is a hands-on, process-driven role suited to someone who is reliable, has a strong work ethic and enjoys working as part of a team. Previous coffee roasting experience is not required, as full training will be provided.

More than anything, we are looking for someone with the right attitude who is willing to learn, comfortable completing repetitive production tasks and looking for a stable, long-term opportunity.

The Role:

Working within an experienced roasting team, your responsibilities will include:

  • Operating coffee roasting and production machinery
  • Following preset recipes and production processes
  • Learning the different stages of the roasting process
  • Entering production data into internal systems and Excel
  • Moving trolleys and handling coffee beans throughout the production area
  • Completing repetitive production tasks accurately and consistently
  • Cleaning equipment and filters
  • Following all safety, quality and production procedures
  • Working closely with supervisors and other members of the production team

About you

We are looking for someone who:

  • Is reliable and takes pride in turning up and doing the job properly
  • Has a positive attitude and is willing to learn
  • Is comfortable working in a repetitive production environment
  • Enjoys hands-on work and operating machinery
  • Can follow processes and instructions accurately
  • Has basic computer skills and is comfortable entering data
  • Works well within a team
  • Communicates well and handles workplace issues professionally
  • Is looking for a long-term permanent opportunity
  • Is comfortable with manual handling, including regular movement of approximately 12kg and occasional lifting up to 24kg

Previous experience within food manufacturing, beverage production, machine operation or general production would be highly regarded, however it is not essential.

Hours:

9am - 5pm or 12pm to 8pm

There may also be occasional paid overtime, generally around one additional hour

Rare weekend work, approximately once per month

Some flexibility required to assist with other shifts when needed

At least one week’s notice provided for planned shift changes where possible

What’s on offer

  • Permanent full-time position
  • Full training provided
  • Supportive and experienced team
  • Opportunity to learn a specialised production skill
  • Long-term career opportunity within food manufacturing

If you are interested in the position please apply with your CV. Feel free to reach Joanna Chen on 0282709757 or email joannac@people2people.com.au.

job.title: Contracts Officer - NSW Government
job.description:
Bring your contract management experience to a role where you'll make a real difference. A NSW Government agency is looking for an experienced Contract Officer to support the review and management of a significant portfolio of contracts associated with a major upcoming NSW event.

Working closely with the Procurement Lead and wider business, you'll play a key role in reviewing existing contractual arrangements, developing contract management plans, and ensuring supplier obligations, deliverables, and compliance requirements are managed effectively. You'll also have the opportunity to work with XAKIA, a new contract management system, helping improve contract visibility, reporting and overall management across the organisation.

What you'll be doing:

  • Reviewing an extensive portfolio of existing contracts, identifying key obligations, deliverables, milestones, expiry dates and contractual requirements.
  • Supporting the ongoing management and administration of NSW Government contracts.
  • Working alongside the Procurement Lead to develop, implement and maintain contract management plans.
  • Monitoring supplier performance, contractual obligations, deliverables and compliance.
  • Identifying contractual risks, gaps and opportunities to improve existing arrangements.
  • Maintaining accurate contract registers, records, documentation and reporting.
  • Using XAKIA to support contract planning, tracking, monitoring and reporting.
  • Partnering with internal stakeholders to ensure contracts are managed effectively and meet business requirements.
  • Assisting with contract variations, renewals, extensions and other contractual matters.

What you'll bring:

  • Demonstrated experience in a Contract Officer, Contract Administrator or Contract Management role.
  • Previous experience working with NSW Government contracts and a sound understanding of government procurement and contract management frameworks.
  • Strong experience reviewing contracts, interpreting contractual obligations and managing contract documentation.
  • An understanding of contract management planning, supplier performance and risk management.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to build relationships across the organisation.
  • Strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple contracts and competing priorities.
  • Confidence using contract management systems and technology. Experience with XAKIA would be advantageous but is not essential.

What's on offer?

  • Initial contract through to June 2027, with a strong possibility of extension through to September 2028 (depending on budget).
  • Hybrid working – 2 days per week in the Sydney CBD office and 3 days working from home.
  • The opportunity to work on a significant NSW Government initiative supporting a major upcoming event.
  • Exposure to a substantial portfolio of government contracts and complex contractual arrangements.
  • The opportunity to work closely with the Procurement Lead and contribute to improving contract management processes and practices.

If you're an experienced Contract Officer who knows your way around NSW Government contracts, enjoys working with detail and takes pride in keeping contractual arrangements organised and on track, this could be your next opportunity. Apply NOW. For further information, please contact Bianca Luck, on 02 8270 9725 or Thulani Tokwe on 02 8270 9736 for a confidential discussion.

job.title: National Technical Support Specialist
job.description:
Oakleigh, Melbourne | Premium Appliance Industry | Newly Created Position

About the Opportunity

A market-leading importer and distributor of premium international appliance brands is seeking a National Technical Support Coordinator to join its growing team.

This newly created role sits at the intersection of technical support, warranty recovery, supplier management and data analysis. Reporting directly to the COO, you'll play a key role in improving technical performance, recovering supplier warranty compensation and supporting a national network of service partners.

This position would suit someone who enjoys combining technical expertise with commercial thinking and stakeholder engagement. One day you might be analysing warranty trends and preparing supplier reports, the next you'll be coordinating service agent training or leading discussions with international manufacturers.

Key Responsibilities

Warranty & Supplier Management

  • Manage the end-to-end warranty claim process
  • Prepare and present claims to international suppliers
  • Track claim approvals, payments and recoveries
  • Lead supplier review meetings and resolve outstanding claims
  • Deliver monthly reporting on warranty recovery performance

Technical Analysis & Reporting

  • Analyse fault trends, service data and warranty performance
  • Monitor parts, labour and recovery costs
  • Provide actionable insights to improve product and service outcomes
  • Support business decision-making through accurate reporting
  • Identify opportunities for continuous improvement across the service network

Service Network Support

  • Coordinate technical training initiatives for service agents
  • Support new product launches through training and technical documentation
  • Distribute technical bulletins, troubleshooting guides and support materials
  • Work closely with product, workshop and after-sales teams to ensure service readiness

Inventory & Write-Off Management

  • Oversee product write-off processes and inventory adjustments
  • Review technical assessments supporting write-off decisions
  • Monitor stock movements and inventory reporting across multiple locations
  • Ensure accurate records and governance are maintained

About You

You will bring:

  • Extensive experience within the appliance, technical service or after-sales environment
  • Strong understanding of warranty management, technical support or service operations
  • Ability to interpret technical fault information and identify trends
  • Experience dealing with suppliers, manufacturers or service partners
  • Strong analytical skills and confidence working with data and reporting
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management capabilities
  • Electrical, Plumbing or Gas qualifications highly regarded
  • Experience with ERP systems and advanced Excel skills preferred

Why Apply?

  • Newly created role with significant influence across the business
  • Direct exposure to executive leadership and strategic projects
  • Work with premium international brands and leading appliance technologies
  • Blend technical expertise with commercial and analytical responsibilities
  • Strong team culture with a genuine focus on continuous improvement
  • Opportunity to make a visible impact on business performance and customer outcomes

Apply Now

If you're a technically minded professional who enjoys analysing data, improving processes and building strong relationships with suppliers and service partners, we'd love to hear from you.

An established importer and distributor of premium international appliance brands is seeking a hands-on Workshop & Technical Supervisor to lead its returns workshop and provide technical leadership across the business.

Mentor and lead workshop technicians and contractors

Foster a culture of continuous improvement and accountability

Extensive experience within the appliance, refrigeration or technical service industry

Previous experience leading technical teams, workshops or service operations

Technical qualifications in Electrical, Plumbing and/or Gas Fitting

Strong understanding of workshop operations, spare parts management and warranty processes

Excellent leadership, communication and stakeholder management skills

Experience working with ERP systems and Microsoft Office applications

The ability to balance hands-on technical work with team leadership responsibilities

Stable, privately owned business with a collaborative culture

Genuine opportunity to make a visible impact across the organisation

job.title: Procurement Lead - NSW Government
job.description:
An exciting opportunity exists for an experienced Procurement Specialist to join a NSW Government agency, supporting the delivery of procurement activities for a major upcoming event.

Reporting to the Senior Commercial Manager, you will work closely with stakeholders across the organisation, providing expert procurement advice and driving complex end-to-end sourcing activities. You will play a key role in developing procurement strategies, managing ICT procurement and establishing supply arrangements to support the successful delivery of this significant event.

What you'll be doing:

  • Leading end-to-end procurement activities, from business needs assessments and market analysis through to sourcing strategy, evaluation, negotiation and contract award.
  • Developing strategic and tactical sourcing strategies to support a major upcoming event.
  • Managing complex ICT procurement activities within the NSW Government ICT Procurement Framework, including ICTA and Core& arrangements.
  • Preparing RFx documentation, leading evaluation processes and preparing evaluation reports and recommendations.
  • Leading contract negotiations and reviewing supply arrangements to achieve strong commercial and value-for-money outcomes.
  • Partnering with stakeholders across the business, providing guidance on procurement, contract management, governance and best practice.
  • Identifying and managing commercial and procurement risks.
  • Ensuring procurement decisions, processes and contractual arrangements are appropriately documented to meet audit, probity and compliance requirements.

What you'll bring:

  • Demonstrated experience managing complex end-to-end procurement activities within a NSW Government department or agency.
  • Strong knowledge of the NSW Government Procurement Framework, NSW Procurement Board Directions and Whole of Government contracts and schemes.
  • Experience across ICT goods and services procurement, with knowledge of ICTA and Core& arrangements highly regarded.
  • Proven expertise in developing procurement strategies, preparing RFx documentation, leading evaluation teams and managing contract negotiations through to award.
  • Strong commercial acumen, with the ability to assess supply markets, identify risks and deliver value-for-money outcomes.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, stakeholder engagement and negotiation skills.
  • The ability to operate as a trusted business partner, influencing stakeholders and providing practical procurement advice.
  • Experience in contract and vendor management, commercial management, contract drafting or procurement transformation initiatives will also be highly regarded.
  • Exposure to strategic procurement and significant commercial outcomes.

If you're an experienced NSW Government Procurement Specialist with a strong background in procurement, this is an opportunity to take on a key role supporting the delivery of a major upcoming event. Offering a competitive daily rate, flexible hybrid working, and the opportunity to lead complex procurement activities, this is a great next contract opportunity for someone looking to make an impact. The team runs the annual Budget process end to end — from developing the Budget Strategy through to delivering the education package on Budget Day. It's high-profile work, internally, for Ministers and within the education sector.

job.title: Chief Executive Officer
job.description:
Chief Executive Officer
Lead the Peak Body for Australia's Strata and Community Titles Sector Strata Community Association (SCA) is the peak industry body representing strata and community title professionals across Australia and New Zealand. Through advocacy, education, professional standards and member engagement, SCA plays a critical role in shaping the future of one of Australia's most significant and rapidly evolving property sectors. Reporting to the Board through the President, the Chief Executive Officer will lead the organisation through its next phase of growth, influence and organisational capability. This is an opportunity for an accomplished executive leader to shape industry outcomes, strengthen member value and drive the strategic direction of a respected national membership organisation.
About the Role
The CEO is responsible for translating Board-approved strategy into disciplined operational delivery while ensuring strong governance, financial sustainability and organisational performance. The role requires sound commercial judgement, political awareness, governance maturity and the ability to lead across a complex national stakeholder environment.
Working closely with the Board, Corporate Members, Chapters, government stakeholders, regulators, sponsors and industry partners, you will:
  • Lead the execution of SCA's strategic plan and annual business priorities
  • Provide high-quality governance support, reporting and strategic advice to the Board
  • Drive financial sustainability and commercial performance across events, sponsorships, education and member services
  • Build trusted relationships across SCA's national federated membership structure
  • Lead advocacy, policy and government engagement initiatives
  • Strengthen professional standards, education and accreditation programs across the sector
  • Develop organisational capability, leadership succession and workforce planning
  • Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration and operational excellence
  • Represent SCA as the trusted and credible national voice for the strata and community titles sector
Key Selection Criteria
To be considered for this opportunity, you will demonstrate:
  • Significant senior executive leadership experience within an industry association, professional body, member organisation, not-for-profit or similarly complex stakeholder environment
  • Proven experience reporting to and working closely with a Board
  • Experience leading within a federated, chapter-based or multi-jurisdictional structure
  • Strong commercial and financial management capability, including budgeting, forecasting and oversight of commercial activities
  • A track record of translating strategy into measurable outcomes through disciplined execution and accountability
  • Outstanding stakeholder management and relationship-building skills
  • Strong judgement, political awareness and the ability to operate effectively within delegated authority
  • Exceptional communication, influencing and leadership capabilities
  • Personal resilience, accountability and a commitment to ethical leadership
  • Experience within industry associations, professional bodies, membership organisations or regulated environments will be highly regarded
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications and/or governance credentials, are also desirable
Applications are invited from accomplished executive leaders with strong governance, financial and stakeholder management capabilities, and proven experience leading in complex stakeholder environments. You will bring sound judgement, resilience and accountability, together with the ability to translate strategy into outcomes and lead through clarity, influence and delivery.
An attractive executive remuneration package, including performance-based incentives, will be negotiated with the successful candidate.
Applications close Friday 14 August.

job.title: SA - SC (5+ PAE) - Commercial Litigation Mixed Disputes
job.description:
A rare opportunity to join a growing Litigation and Dispute Resolution team within a leading national commercial practice. This role offers complex disputes work, real courtroom exposure and clear pathways for development across Associate, Senior Associate and Special Counsel levels.

The Firm

This national law firm is recognised for its high quality commercial disputes practice, supportive leadership and commitment to structured career development. The firm offers the discipline and complexity of a large practice while maintaining an approachable, collaborative culture. With strong internal processes, a junior heavy team and a strategic growth plan, the firm provides stability, excellent resources and a workplace where technical excellence is valued. Twice yearly performance reviews, transparent promotions and access to modern legal technology, including AI driven tools, support long term growth.

The Role

Due to expansion, the firm is seeking multiple hires at Associate, Senior Associate and Special Counsel level. Working full time in the Sydney office, the successful candidates will:

  • Manage a broad portfolio of commercial litigation including contract disputes, competition and consumer law matters, corporate disputes, banking and finance litigation, IP disputes and large scale debt recovery.
  • Draft complex affidavits, submissions, evidence and correspondence.
  • Lead contested interlocutory applications and engage with NSW courts.
  • Mentor junior lawyers and contribute to a high performing team environment.
  • Apply disciplined time recording, document protocols and matter management processes.
  • Collaborate closely with senior principals while maintaining autonomy on files.
  • Focus on delivering high quality litigation outcomes, with BD expectations remaining low.

Insolvency and class action focused backgrounds are not aligned with the needs of this team.

The Candidate

The ideal candidate will demonstrate:

  • Between 3+ years PAE in commercial litigation.
  • Background in a mid tier or top tier environment with exposure to complex matters.
  • Strong drafting skills and confidence with contested interlocutory work.
  • NSW litigation experience including familiarity with relevant legislation and court procedures.
  • A calm, senior presence with the ability to mentor and develop junior team members.
  • Career stability and commitment to full time in office work (with some WFH flexibility following probation).
  • Excellent communication skills and a collaborative attitude.
  • Alignment with a team that values high standards, technical rigour and a supportive culture.

Benefits

The firm provides an extensive suite of benefits across career growth, flexibility, wellbeing, training and social engagement, including:

  • Industry memberships, postgraduate study support and a formal pro bono program
  • Structured development pathways including Mentoring and Leadership, Senior Associate and Special Counsel Pathway, Principal Pathway and Women in Leadership
  • Flexible work policies including parental leave, remote working options and occasional access to national offices

job.title: Customs Broker - Air
job.description:
Western Suburbs, Melbourne VIC

Up to $120,000 + Super

Hybrid Working Available

About the Company

people2people are partnering with a well-established global logistics and freight forwarding organisation to recruit a Licensed Customs Broker for their Melbourne operation.

With a strong international presence and a reputation for investing in their people, this organisation continues to experience steady growth across its customs function. As a result of increasing volume and future growth plans, they are looking to expand their customs team with the addition of another broker.

This is an excellent opportunity to join a business that combines the resources and stability of a global organisation with the support and collaboration of a close-knit local team.

The Opportunity

Working within a supportive customs team, you will be responsible for the end-to-end customs clearance process, ensuring all import and export declarations are completed accurately and in accordance with Australian customs regulations.

Key responsibilities include:

Preparing and lodging import and export declarations

Tariff classification and customs compliance

Managing customs holds, inspections and quarantine requirements

Reviewing shipping and customs documentation

Liaising with freight forwarders, transport providers and regulatory authorities

Providing advice and guidance on customs requirements

Maintaining accurate records and ensuring compliance standards are met

Supporting continuous improvement within the customs function

You'll be joining a team that already has compiler and offshore support in place, allowing brokers to focus on value-added customs activities rather than excessive administrative tasks.

The successful candidate will be given the opportunity to develop their skills while working alongside highly experienced customs professionals in a collaborative environment that encourages learning, knowledge sharing and professional growth.

About You

To be successful, you will have:

A current Australian Customs Broker Licence

Experience within customs brokerage, customs clearance or freight forwarding

Strong knowledge of customs compliance and tariff classifications

Excellent attention to detail

The ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment

Strong communication and stakeholder management skills

Experience with CargoWise is highly regarded but not essential.

Importantly, our client is open to considering both newly licensed and experienced brokers. If you hold a current licence and are looking for a business where you can continue to develop your career, we encourage you to apply.

We're looking for someone who values teamwork, takes pride in the quality of their work, demonstrates sound judgement, and understands the importance of integrity within the customs industry. This role will suit someone who enjoys contributing to a positive team environment and building strong working relationships with colleagues and stakeholders alike.

What's on Offer?

Salary package of up to $120,000 + Super

Annual bonus program

Hybrid working arrangement available following onboarding and training

Structured onboarding and training programs

Ongoing professional development opportunities, including dedicated personal development training

Supportive leadership and mentorship from experienced industry professionals

Regular team catch-ups and development discussions

Employee recognition initiatives and team events

Long-term career development within a growing global organisation

If you're a Licensed Customs Broker looking to join a business that values collaboration, professional development and long-term career growth, we'd love to hear from you.

job.title: Senior Policy Advisor
job.description:
Te whiwhinga mahi | The Opportunity

Join a central government policy team working in the intelligence space. This is a close-knit, recently rebuilt team of good humour and genuine collegiality, where the work is varied, topical and consequential. You will be part of a group that provides sharp, timely second-opinion policy advice on some of the country's most significant public safety questions.

He aha koe e whiwhi ai? | What's in it for you?

  • Salary band of $142,124 – $181,603, with a midpoint of $157,916
  • A genuinely well-regarded salary band for a senior policy position
  • One day per week working from home, negotiable by agreement once you are settled
  • A broad portfolio — so no two pieces of work look alike
  • A nice working environment with good colleagues, good humour and interesting work
  • Support to obtain a national security clearance if you do not already hold one

Kōrero mō te tūranga | About the Role

This is a senior policy position for a practitioner who enjoys breadth. You will work across at least three major strategic national security initiatives in the coming year, alongside ongoing legislative work and emerging online issues. Much of the team's work is second-opinion policy advice — the same rigour as developing policy from scratch, delivered in far less time. You will also play a visible role in lifting the capability of a team with many early-career members.

Ngā kawenga | Key Responsibilities

  • Provide high-quality second-opinion policy advice across intelligence portfolios
  • Develop, test and critique policy proposals to a high standard under tight timeframes
  • Contribute thought leadership to major strategic national security initiatives
  • Support legislative and regulatory work
  • Analyse emerging technology challenges, including online harm to children and young people
  • Build and manage relationships with policy and operational colleagues across agencies
  • Present and advocate the team's position credibly to central policy agencies
  • Mentor, coach and support more junior and early-career members of the team

Ngā pūkenga me ngā wheako | Skills & Experience

  • A very experienced policy practitioner — principal, chief advisor, manager or experienced contractor background, or a strong senior ready for the next step
  • A capable generalist who can turn their hand to a variety of subject matter
  • Proven critical thinking and thought leadership on substantial policy work
  • Excellent relationship management and the ability to present messages persuasively
  • Experience mentoring and coaching less experienced policy staff
  • Holds a national security clearance, or is able to obtain one, with a verifiable history and the maturity the clearance requires
  • Knowledge of the national security sector is helpful; strong transferable skills are welcome

Me pēwhea te tuku tono | How to apply

Apply now with your current CV.
